name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about nineteen points Republican and Meuser is the incumbent
Prediction markets price the race around 96 percent Republican
Wallace holds a modest cash-on-hand edge, but outside spending is negligible
No public general-election polling is available
model.rationale: The district's nineteen-point Republican lean, Meuser's incumbency, and prediction markets pricing the race near 96 percent Republican leave little room for an upset, even though Wallace slightly outpaces him in cash on hand after his primary spending.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or credible polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signal that the margin could compress.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
PA-09 is a heavily Republican district in northeastern Pennsylvania, and Republican Dan Meuser is seeking another term as the incumbent. The fundamentals point firmly his way: the district leans about nineteen points Republican, the national environment favors the GOP, and prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. No public general-election polling is available for this race.

Democrat Rachel Wallace has run a credible campaign, slightly edging Meuser in cash on hand after he spent heavily to secure renomination. Still, outside spending has been negligible, no major rating organizations list the race as competitive, and the structural advantage of incumbency in a seat this lean is difficult to overcome. The forecast expects Meuser to win by a wide margin, with Wallace needing a dramatic shift in the political environment to make this competitive.
